title: Authorization schema migration — staged shadow writes, deterministic backfills, and operations cutover playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Replace the current authorization store and runtime mappings (RBAC v1) with the new v2 schema and runtime while preserving audit continuity, SSO/SAML mappings, and admin UX. This ticket covers the migration strategy, safe dual-write and shadow write modes, deterministic sharded backfill algorithm, reconciliation tooling, cutover gating, rollback criteria, and customer-facing comms. Scope includes data model transforms, streaming audit preservation, SSO mapping fallback, admin console feature flags, and runbook for day-of cutover.
acceptance_criteria: All orgs can operate on v2 semantics in shadow mode with zero functional regressions during canary window
Backfill jobs complete for 95% of tenants within target window (<= 6 hours for small tenants, <= 72 hours for largest tenants) with <0.01% error rate
Audit log continuity preserved: every v1 authorization decision has a corresponding v2 audit entry (traceable by audit_id)
SSO/SAML mapping tests pass for sampled enterprise tenants in canary group
Observable reconciliation: reconciliation pipeline identifies and repairs drift within defined SLOs
Rollback path validated via synthetic dry-run and tested on staging with <10 minute recovery time
tasks: Implement tenant-sharded deterministic backfill job (Engineering: Diego)
Dual-write shim for write path with tombstone and version tags (Engineering: Jinsoo)
Reconciliation service 3-pass: snapshot, delta-apply, targeted repair (Eng: Priya)
Audit stream transformation to preserve audit_id and original decision payload (Eng: Sasha)
SSO mapping validation harness (Auth team: Marco)
Admin console feature-flag + rollout controls (Frontend: Lina)
Canary orchestration and traffic-splitting policy (SRE: Omar)
Customer comms and opt-in/opt-out self-service page (PM: Elena)
End-to-end chaos tests for in-flight requests and KV cache hot paths (QA: Raj)
runbook_steps: Pre-cutover checklist: confirm reconciliation jobs healthy, SSO smoke tests green, audit stream consumer replicas at desired lag
Enable dual-write in shadow mode for canary orgs (10% of traffic) with verbose audit logging
Run deterministic backfill in shards: pre-warm cache for each shard, run low-priority workers, validate counts against snapshot
Monitor reconciliation metrics; if drift > 0.1% for canary orgs, pause and investigate
Escalation window: if error rate on canary increases > 2x baseline, auto-fail to v1 via runtime flag
Progressively widen canary to 50% after 48h stable, then full rollout over 72h with throttled backfill concurrency
Final cutover: switch authoritative read path to v2 once reconciliation <0.01% drift and audit continuity verified
Post-cutover: retain v1 read replicas in read-only mode for 14 days, continue reconciliation snapshot every 6h for 7 days
Rollback: enable runtime fallback, drain new writes to v2, rehydrate v1 authoritative store from latest snapshot if needed
risks: Large orgs with millions of permission rows may cause backfill hotspots — mitigated via tenant sharding and rate limiting
Reconciliation false-positives due to eventual consistency windows — mitigated by deterministic snapshot windows and idempotent repair actions
SSO mapping edge-cases for legacy SAML assertions — mitigated by fallback to attribute-mapping and customer opt-in testing
Audit discontinuity if transformation pipeline drops correlation IDs — mitigation: preserve audit_id and replay from raw Kafka topic to S3 archive
Operator error during cutover toggles — mitigation: gating UI and approval step + 2-person approval for global rollout
